faqs.a: The click-speed pad counts each press for exactly 5 seconds, so 30 clicks equals 6.0 clicks per second. Most people land between 4 and 7 CPS. Gamers with drag-click or butterfly techniques can reach 10 or more.
faqs.q: How is CPS (clicks per second) calculated?

faqs.a: Open this page in another browser or app. If it works there, the first app was swallowing the event. If it fails everywhere, check the switch, cable, or wireless receiver - and try another USB port.
faqs.q: One button does not register anywhere. What now?

faqs.a: It can be the wheel encoder wearing out, dust inside the mouse, or the app ignoring small scroll steps. If scrolling fails in this page too, the hardware is suspect; if it works here, the app is filtering the input.
faqs.q: My scroll wheel skips or jumps. Is it broken?

faqs.a: Probably not - the browser just sees a press. What can look like lag is the OS double-click speed setting, which decides how close together two clicks must be to count as a double-click. Adjust it in your OS mouse settings.
faqs.q: Double-clicks feel slow. Is my mouse lagging?

mouse-tester.formula:
CPS (clicks per second) = total clicks / 5 seconds.
Example: 32 clicks in 5 seconds = 32 / 5 = 6.4 CPS.
Scroll balance = |scroll up - scroll down| should be close to 0 for even scrolling.
howTo: Press each button on your mouse inside the button pads. Each pad flashes and counts its presses.
For click speed: press the big pad once to start the 5-second timer, then click as fast as you can.
Double-click the double-click pad. Each recognised double-click adds one to the counter.
Scroll up and down inside the scroll zone to test both wheel directions.
Compare up vs down counts - they should be close if the wheel is healthy.
keyFacts: Mice report button codes: 0 = left, 1 = middle (wheel click), 2 = right, 3 = back, 4 = forward.
A button that never flashes here is either physically broken or blocked by another app.
CPS = total clicks divided by 5 seconds. 4 to 7 CPS is normal; above 10 is very fast.
Scroll events carry a direction (deltaY): negative means up, positive means down.
Right-click is suppressed on this page so the browser menu does not interrupt your test.
Double-click detection uses your OS timing setting, so the same hardware can feel different on two computers.

mouse-tester.quickAnswer: A mouse tester checks all five standard buttons (left, middle, right, back, forward), measures your click speed in a 5-second test, counts double-clicks, and verifies the scroll wheel in both directions. If a button pad flashes and counts up, that button works. The click-speed result is total clicks divided by 5, giving clicks per second.
mouse-tester.tagline: Test every mouse button, measure your click speed, and check the scroll wheel.
mouse-tester.workedExample:
You run the click-speed test:
1. You press the pad. The 5-second timer starts.
2. You click as fast as you can: the counter reaches 32.
3. The timer ends. CPS = 32 / 5 = 6.4 clicks per second.
4. Your best score so far updates to 6.4.
Then you test the wheel: 40 scroll-up events and 41 scroll-down events - even, so the wheel is healthy.
